---
title: "Nothing gets printed inside a for loop"
ref: FLW-06
categories: [Control flow]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'for (i in 1:2) i'
attendu: "`[1] 1` then `[1] 2`"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
for (i in 1:2) {
  i
  i * 10
}

compute <- function(x) {
  x + 1
  x * 2
}
compute(5)
```
:::

## Why

At the console, R prints the value of every statement typed at the top level: this is auto-printing. A `for` loop is a single statement, which invisibly returns `NULL`. The values computed inside it are never printed.

A function does no better: only its last value is returned, and therefore printed. `x + 1` is computed, then lost. The same pitfall hits {ggplot2} plots created in a loop, which do not show up without `print()`.

## The fix

Ask for printing explicitly with `print()`, or store the results in a vector.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
for (i in 1:2) {
  print(i * 10)
}

results <- vapply(1:2, FUN = function(i) {
  i * 10
}, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
results
```
:::
